newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris Hard Rock Cafe denies using British beef.
newsitem.headline: Paris Hard Rock Cafe denies using British beef.

text.p: French police accused the Hard Rock Cafe in Paris on Thursday of using British beef in defiance of a ban imposed over the mad cow crisis -- but the restaurant said the meat came legally from Irish cows.

Police said health inspectors found 300 kg (660 lbs) of frozen hamburgers during a routine health check this week at the restaurant on the Boulevard Montmartre, one of an American-style chain owned by the Rank Organisation.
"The batch of frozen minced beef had a stamp indicating an English origin," Jean Jamet, head of veterinary services at Paris police headquarters, told Reuters.
The Hard Rock Cafe rejected the charges.

"The meat is Irish," it said in a statement, saying Irish beef was not affected by any ban in France. "The Hard Rock Cafe has favoured Irish meat for a long time for all its outlets in Europe because of its high quality."
It said the confusion arose because the meat had passed through a processing centre in Britain, dealing exclusively with Irish products, and which had "all necessary permits to export to Europe".
It said it met the veterinary officials at Paris police headquarters on Thursday and promised to provide documentation by November 5 to prove the meat conformed to French law.

France led a worldwide ban on imports of British beef in March over fears that mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could be passed to humans. BSE is most widespread in Britain.
If the police managed to prove their charges, the restaurant could risk a temporary closure and importers could face legal action.
